# FAQ-014 Engineering FAQ #14

Revision: Rev A

Q1 — What lubricant should be used for the Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02), and where is it stocked?
A1 — The lubricant part number for Heat Treat heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L4-HT02) is CFW-LUB-426. Background: CFW-LUB-426 was selected for its high-temperature stability and low carbonization characteristics appropriate to furnace internal bearings and slideways. Rationale: Using the specified part number prevents chemical incompatibility with furnace insulation and avoids accelerated deposit formation. Example use: apply CFW-LUB-426 to furnace door guide rails after cleaning with approved solvent and prior to cyclic loading. Records to keep: log part number used, batch/lot code from the lubricant container, application location (furnace ID), and the operator initials in the maintenance record. See also ECN-2026-033 for the approval history and MM-P2-L3-HT02 for heat treat lubrication procedures.

Q2 — What torque value is required for the main ram bolt on Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01)?
A2 — The main ram bolt torque for Hot Forge hydraulic forging press #1 (EQ-P3-L1-HP01) is 1425 N·m. Background: This is the assembly torque established during press rebuild and verified by engineering stress analysis. Rationale: Applying the specified 1425 N·m ensures pre-load consistent with the press design and prevents cyclic loosening or fatigue failure of the fastener. Example procedure: torque the main ram bolt using a calibrated torque tool capable of reading the specified value; confirm calibration traceability in tool records. Records to keep: record the applied torque value, torque tool ID and calibration certificate reference, operator initials, and the maintenance work order. Refer to SB-1016 for bolt inspection acceptance criteria and ECN-2026-033 for any historical changes to assembly requirements.

Q3 — Which lubricant is specified for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02)?
A3 — The lubricant part number for Machining CNC turning center #2 (EQ-P3-L3-CN02) is CFW-LUB-611. Background: CFW-LUB-611 is specified for spindle and guideway systems where low-viscosity, anti-wear properties are required. Rationale: Specifying CFW-LUB-611 avoids cross-contamination with other lubricant families that may degrade seals or bearings. Example use: during scheduled bearing service, drain the existing lubricant following the machining center procedure, flush as required, and apply CFW-LUB-611 to the spindle and guide components. Records to keep: maintenance action recorded in the asset history, lubricant part number and container lot, quantity used, and technician initials. See MM-P2-L3-HT02 for general lubrication controls and ECN-2026-033 for procurement approvals.

Q4 — What is the austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02)?
A4 — The austenitizing setpoint for Machining heat treat furnace #2 (EQ-P2-L3-HT02) is 845 °C. Background: The 845 °C austenitizing setpoint matches the process requirements for the tool steels commonly processed in Machining heat treatment and was validated during process qualification. Rationale: Maintaining the specified 845 °C setpoint is required to achieve the metallurgical phase transformation targets and final mechanical properties. Example control: verify setpoint programming in the furnace controller prior to a run, execute the documented temperature ramp and hold profile, and confirm with calibrated thermocouple readings as part of the process control records. Records to keep: furnace controller program settings, thermocouple verification data, lot identifier of charges processed, and process operator sign-off. See MM-P2-L3-HT02 for heat treat procedure details and ECN-2026-033 for formal setpoint approval documentation.

Q5 — What is the shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03), and how should top-up be performed?
A5 — The shot media top-up interval for Hot Forge shot blast cabinet #3 (EQ-P2-L1-SB03) is 33 hours. Background: The 33 hours top-up interval reflects operational experience balancing media degradation, dust generation, and cabinet throughput. Rationale: Regular top-up at the interval prevents abrasive deficiency that can reduce cleaning effectiveness and increases media condition consistency across parts. Example procedure: at the end of the specified operating interval, inspect media cleanliness and size distribution, add approved shot media to restore working volume, and screen/remove fines as necessary. Records to keep: top-up event timestamp, media lot/grade, quantity added, pre- and post-top-up media inspection notes, cabinet ID, and operator initials. Consult SB-1016 for abrasive handling guidance and ECN-2026-033 for any changes to shot media specification.

Related documents
- ECN-2026-033
- MM-P2-L3-HT02
- SB-1016
